title: Build header-name-based column mapping engine for premium Excel parsing
description: Replace hardcoded positional column access (values[1]-[5]) with a header-name-based column mapping engine that reads Excel row 1 headers and maps them to internal fields. Create a column configuration registry per input_type so that each premium type knows its required and optional columns. Support blok input_type columns: empcode, gang_code, subblok, jumlah, jenis as Phase 1 scope.

files.change: Replace ALLOWED_JENIS constant and positional row parsing with header-name-based mapping engine. Add ColumnMappingConfig interface and buildColumnMapping() function. Add parseRowByHeaders() replacing eachRow callback that reads column names from row 1.

Add PremiumColumnMapping, PremiumImportRow (generalized with optional fields per input_type), ColumnMappingRegistry types. Define blok column config: required=[empcode,subblok,jumlah], optional=[gang_code,jenis].

implementation: Define ColumnMappingConfig interface with required_cols, optional_cols, and header_aliases per input_type
Create input_type_column_configs registry mapping blok/exp/kendaraan/blok+exp/amount to their column sets
Implement buildColumnMapping(): read row 1 values, match header names (case-insensitive, trimmed) to config fields, return Map<fieldName, columnIndex>
Implement parseRowByHeaders(): accepts row values + column mapping, returns typed PremiumImportRow with all mapped fields
Add resolveHeaderName() helper for fuzzy matching (trim, uppercase, collapse spaces, strip prefixes)
Validate that all required columns are present; collect missing column errors
Handle blok-specific fields: subblok maps from ['subblok', 'blok', 'block'], gang_code from ['gang_code', 'gang', 'regu'], jumlah from ['jumlah', 'amount', 'total', 'nominal']

reference.pattern: Header-name-based mapping with alias support, similar to DynamicColumnDetector.ts L64-L73 header normalization pattern
reference.examples: Existing premiumImportService.ts L48-L75 shows current positional parsing that must be replaced. premiumDefinitionService.ts L21 defines PremiumInputType union. manualAdjustmentNaming.ts L15-L20 shows normalization pattern for name matching.

criteria: Column mapping correctly resolves all 5 blok columns (empcode, gang_code, subblok, jumlah, jenis) from header row regardless of column order
Missing required columns produce clear error messages listing which columns are absent
Fuzzy header matching handles variants: 'Emp Code'/'empcode'/'EMP_CODE' all map to empcode field
parseRowByHeaders() returns PremiumImportRow objects with all fields populated from correct columns
Unit test with 3 different column orderings produces identical PremiumImportRow arrays

rationale.chosen_approach: Header-name-based mapping with alias registry per input_type. Row 1 treated as header row, column names matched against known aliases for each field. Resolves fragility of positional access and supports varying column layouts across divisions.
alternatives_considered: Fixed positional columns per premium type in premium_definitions.json
Hybrid: core columns positional, premium-specific columns header-mapped
decision_factors: Flexibility: different divisions may have different column orders
Maintainability: single mapping engine vs per-type position configs
User experience: field operators should not need to reorder columns
rationale.tradeoffs: Slightly more complex row parsing logic. Requires header row always present in row 1. Must handle empty/missing optional columns gracefully.

manual_checks: Parse Excel with reordered columns (empcode in col E, jumlah in col A) and verify correct mapping
Parse Excel with extra unrecognized columns and verify no errors on extra columns
Parse Excel missing 'subblok' column and verify clear error message
success_metrics: 100% of required columns detected when present in any column position
0 false positives on column name matching
Clear error messages for all 5 required columns when missing
